artifact.self_contained_problem:
Prove or disprove the following two statements.

(i) Let $p$ be a prime and $a$ a positive integer with $p^a \equiv 1 \pmod 3$. Then
$$\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor 2p^a/3 \rfloor} (21k+8)\binom{2k}{k}^{3} \;\equiv\; 8\,p^a \pmod{p^{\,a+5+(-1)^p}},$$
where the modulus exponent is $a+6$ when $p$ is odd and $a+4$ when $p=2$.

(ii) If an integer $n>1$ satisfies
$$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} (21k+8)\binom{2k}{k}^{3} \;\equiv\; 8n \pmod{n^{4}},$$
then $n$ is prime.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is part of Zhi-Wei Sun's series of supercongruence conjectures involving sums of (21k+8)·C(2k,k)^3. While related results (e.g., integrality of the average and weaker mod p^4 supercongruences) have been established, the strengthened modulus in part (i) and the primality characterization in part (ii) do not appear to have been proven in the literature; they are still listed among Sun's open conjectures.

status_evidence.title: Super congruences and Euler numbers (arXiv:1001.4453)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses related supercongruences modulo p^4 for sums involving (21k+8)C(2k,k)^3 but leaves Sun's stronger conjectures open.
status_evidence.claim: Related weaker congruences proved; the stronger modulus and converse remain conjectural.

status_evidence.title: Notes on conjectures of Zhi-Wei Sun
status_evidence.snippet: Lists Sun's supercongruence conjectures including the (21k+8)C(2k,k)^3 family.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is catalogued among Sun's open conjectures.
